Definition: from the base of G4628; warped, i.e. winding; figuratively, perverse:--crooked, froward, untoward.
BiblicalUsage: Skolios means crooked, warped, perverse, and it describes a generation and a road. Peter tells the crowd to save themselves from this untoward generation, Paul tells the Philippians to shine as lights among a crooked and perverse nation, and Isaiah promises the crooked shall be made straight and the rough ways smooth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the crooked generation is still with us. I hold that the straight road is the one the Lord Himself makes level for His people.
